title: Split solver from an exact unary source
statement: Let $C,e$ be natural numbers, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $M$, and let $B:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean word $s$, starting from the configuration with state $a$, empty output, and every work tape holding the unary word of length $|s|+1$, the machine reaches after exactly $B(|s|)$ steps the halted configuration with output consisting of $C(|s|+1)^e$ ones and the same tape contents. Suppose also that $B(l)\le (C+1+5e)(l+1)^e+1$ for every natural number $l$. Then some finite Turing machine computes, on every Boolean word $w$, the encoded pair of the prefix and suffix at the least $i\in\{0,\ldots,|w|\}$ satisfying $i+C(i+1)^e=|w|$, or the empty word if no such $i$ exists, in at most $c(|w|+1)^{e+2}$ steps for some natural number $c$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$B$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
For every Boolean word $s$, the specified unary-bank computation reaches the stated halted configuration after exactly $B(|s|)$ steps
replaced:
Let a source machine, started on the prepared bank for any candidate $s$,
halt within $B(\abs{s})$ steps with captured output a run of
$C\,(\abs{s}+1)^{e}$ ones, where $B(l) \le (C+1+5e)(l+1)^{e} + 1$. Then there
exist a machine $N$ and a constant $c$ computing, within $c\,(n+1)^{e+2}$
steps, the function sending $w$ to the pair encoding of the split of $w$ at
the least $i$ with $i + C\,(i+1)^{e} = \abs{w}$, and to the empty word when
no such $i$ exists.
